Xianzong confronted Deng in person, learned the truth, was greatly enraged, and was about to execute Qun; Jifu pleaded for him and he was spared, being sent out as Huainan observation commissioner.
Xianzong confronted Deng in person, learned the truth, was greatly enraged, and was about to execute Qun; Jifu pleaded for him and he was spared, being sent out as Hunan observation commissioner.
Chinese 出為湖南觀察使 names Hunan (湖南), not Huainan (淮南, which belongs to Jifu in s0026); the literal’s Huainan is a place-name error, and the proposed Hunan matches both the Chinese and the idiomatic.

Ku, style name Zhouqing, died as prefect of Wuzhou.
Chinese 終婺州刺史 is prefect of Wuzhou (婺州); bare Wu drops the prefecture name and is inaccurate, so Wuzhou is the correct repair.
Ku, styled Zhouqing, ended as prefect of Wu.
Ku, styled Zhouqing, ended as prefect of Wuzhou.
The literal likewise truncates 婺州 to Wu; ending as prefect of Wuzhou restores the full place name without other changes.

Youxin, with Reminder Li Xu and Liu Qichu, were Fengji's attack dogs and were hated for it, hence the label "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."

為逢吉搏吠所憎 means Youxin and company were detested as Fengji’s barking attack dogs (they were the attackers), not hated by Fengji’s pack; the proposed literal reverses that agency error and matches the idiomatic sense.

When Fengji lost office and went to the Shannan East Circuit, he took Youxin as campaign Sima.
Chinese 領山南東道節度 is the Shannan East Circuit command; Huainan (淮南) is a different circuit, so replacing Huainan east circuit with Shannan East Circuit corrects the place name.
When Fengji fell from power and took the Huainan east circuit command, he had Youxin as his campaign staff Sima.
When Fengji fell from power and took the Shannan East Circuit command, he had Youxin as his campaign staff Sima.
The literal’s Huainan east circuit likewise misreads 山南東道; Shannan East Circuit command is the accurate place-name repair.

Implicated in Tian Pi's case, he was demoted to prefect of Ting.
田伾 is Tian Pi (伾 Pī); You is a misreading of 伾, and the proposed idiomatic corrects only that personal name.
For involvement in Tian You's affair he was demoted to prefect of Ting.
For involvement in Tian Pi's affair he was demoted to prefect of Ting.
The literal also has Tian You for 田伾; Tian Pi matches the character and pinyin, and the rest of the sentence is unchanged.

Ning passed the Mingjing, served as Linhuan chief clerk, quit office, returned home to Xia, and became Yang Cheng's closest friend.

He passed the Mingjing examination, was appointed chief clerk of Linhuan, resigned, returned to Xia, and became sworn friend with Yang Cheng.
The literal likewise misreads 臨渙 as Linhuai; chief clerk of Linhuan restores the correct county name.

貶漳州司戶參軍 is demotion to Zhangzhou (漳州); Qiongzhou would be 瓊州, so Zhangzhou is the correct place-name repair.

units.zh: 竇劉二張楊熊柏
units.en: Dou, Liu, the two Zhangs, Yang, Xiong, and Bai
units.literal: Dou, Liu, the two Zhangs, Yang, Xiong, and Bai

units.zh: 竇群，字丹列，京兆金城人。
units.en: Dou Qun, whose style name was Danlie, came from Jincheng in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Dou Qun, styled Danlie, was a native of Jincheng in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 父叔向，以詩自名，代宗時，位左拾遺。
units.en: His father Shuxiang was famed for his verse; under Emperor Daizong he served as Left Reminder.
units.literal: His father Shuxiang made a name for himself through poetry; in Emperor Daizong's reign he held the post of Left Reminder.

units.zh: 群兄弟皆擢進士第，獨群以處士客隱毗陵。
units.en: All of Qun's brothers won the jinshi degree; he alone lived as a retired scholar in hiding at Piling.
units.literal: Qun's brothers all passed the jinshi examination, but Qun alone, as a reclusive gentleman, lodged in seclusion at Piling.

units.zh: 母卒，嚙一指置棺中，廬墓次，終喪。
units.en: At his mother's death he severed a finger and laid it in her coffin, dwelt in a mourning hut by the grave, and completed the full mourning rites.
units.literal: When his mother died, he bit off one finger and placed it in the coffin, kept vigil beside the tomb, and observed the full mourning period.

units.zh: 從盧庇傳啖助《春秋》學，著書數十篇。
units.en: He followed Lu Pi in the Tan Zhu school of Spring and Autumn studies and composed several dozen works.
units.literal: He studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Lu Pi, who transmitted the teachings of Tan Zhu, and wrote several dozen treatises.

units.zh: 蘇州刺史韋夏卿薦之朝，並表其書，報聞，不召。
units.en: Prefect Wei Xiaqing of Suzhou recommended him to the throne and submitted his books together with the recommendation; the court took note but did not call him in.
units.literal: Suzhou prefect Wei Xiaqing recommended him to court and jointly memorialized his writings; the court acknowledged receipt but did not summon him.

units.zh: 後夏卿入為京兆尹，復言之德宗，擢為左拾遺。
units.en: When Xiaqing later became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, he spoke for him again to Dezong, who appointed him Left Reminder.
units.literal: Later, when Xiaqing entered the capital as metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, he spoke of him again to Emperor Dezong, who promoted him to Left Reminder.

units.zh: 時張薦持節使吐蕃，乃遷群侍御史，為薦判官，入見帝曰：「陛下即位二十年，始自草茅擢臣為拾遺，何其難也？
units.en: When Zhang Jian held credentials as envoy to Tibet, Qun was moved to Attending Censor and made his judicial aide. He appeared before the emperor and said, "Sire, in twenty years on the throne you have only now lifted me from the thatched hut to Reminder—how rare such advancement is!
units.literal: At that time Zhang Jian was commissioner to Tibet; Qun was transferred to Attending Censor and made Jian's aide. On entering audience he said to the emperor: "Your Majesty, in the twenty years since you took the throne you have only now raised me from common obscurity to Reminder—how hard that was!

units.zh: 以二十年難進之臣為和蕃判官，一何易？」
units.en: Yet you would make a man you found so hard to promote over twenty years the aide for a Tibetan peace mission—how lightly you treat such a post!"
units.literal: Yet to make a man so hard to advance over twenty years the judicial aide for pacifying Tibet—how easy that is!"

units.zh: 帝壯其言，不遣。
units.en: The emperor was stirred by his remonstrance and did not dispatch him.
units.literal: The emperor was impressed by his words and did not send him.

units.zh: 王叔文黨盛，雅不喜群，群亦悻悻不肯附。
units.en: Wang Shuwen's party was ascendant and had little regard for Qun; Qun in turn sullenly refused to join them.
units.literal: Wang Shuwen's faction was powerful and naturally disliked Qun; Qun too was resentful and unwilling to attach himself.

units.zh: 欲逐之，韋執誼不可，乃止。
units.en: They wanted to expel him, but Wei Zhiyi objected, and the plan was dropped.
units.literal: They wished to drive him out, but Wei Zhiyi would not agree, and the matter stopped there.

units.zh: 群往見叔文曰：「事有不可知者。」
units.en: Qun went to Shuwen and said, "Some things cannot be foreseen."
units.literal: Qun went to see Shuwen and said, "There are matters one cannot foresee."

units.zh: 叔文曰：「奈何？」
units.en: Shuwen asked, "What do you mean?"
units.literal: Shuwen said, "What then?"

units.zh: 曰：「去年李實伐恩恃權，震赫中外，君此時逡巡路傍，江南一吏耳。
units.en: He replied, "Last year Li Shi abused grace and monopolized authority, terrifying the empire; you were then hesitating on the roadside—no more than a petty official south of the Yangtze.
units.literal: He said, "Last year Li Shi relied on favor and wielded power, shaking court and realm; you then lingered by the roadside—a mere clerk of south of the Yangtze.

units.zh: 今君又處實之勢，豈不思路傍復有如君者乎？」
units.en: Now you occupy Shi's place—have you not thought that someone like you may again be waiting by the roadside?"
units.literal: Now you stand in Shi's position—will you not consider that by the roadside there may again be someone like you?"

units.zh: 叔文悚然，亦卒不用。
units.en: Shuwen was shaken, and in the end never used him.
units.literal: Shuwen was startled, and in the end did not employ him.

units.zh: 憲宗立，轉膳部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事。
units.en: Under Emperor Xianzong he became Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Attending Censor with charge of miscellaneous business.
units.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, Qun was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites and concurrently Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters.

units.zh: 出為唐州刺史。
units.en: He was sent out as prefect of Tangzhou.
units.literal: He went out as prefect of Tangzhou.

units.zh: 節度使於頔聞其名，與語，奇之，表以自副。
units.en: Military commissioner Yu Di, hearing of him, conversed with him, marveled at him, and requested him as personal aide.
units.literal: The military commissioner Yu Di heard his reputation, spoke with him, found him extraordinary, and memorialized to have him as his deputy.

units.zh: 武元衡、李吉甫皆所厚善，故召拜吏部郎中。
units.en: Wu Yuanheng and Li Jifu both favored him, and he was recalled as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: Wu Yuanheng and Li Jifu were both well disposed toward him, so he was summoned and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 元衡輔政，薦群代為中丞。
units.en: Yuanheng, as chief minister, recommended Qun to replace him as censor-in-chief.
units.literal: When Yuanheng served as chief minister, he recommended Qun to succeed him as censor-in-chief.

units.zh: 群引呂溫、羊士諤為御史，吉甫以二人躁險，持不下。
units.en: Qun nominated Lü Wen and Yang Shie as censors; Jifu judged them reckless and would not confirm them.
units.literal: Qun brought in Lü Wen and Yang Shie as censors; Jifu regarded the two as rash and dangerous and withheld approval.

units.zh: 群忮狠，反怨吉甫。
units.en: Qun was spiteful and turned his resentment on Jifu.
units.literal: Qun was jealous and fierce, and turned to resent Jifu.

units.zh: 吉甫節度淮南，群謂失恩，因擠之。
units.en: When Jifu went out to Huainan as military commissioner, Qun thought he had fallen from grace and worked to squeeze him out.
units.literal: When Jifu was made military commissioner of Huainan, Qun believed he had lost favor and pressed against him.

units.zh: 陳登者，善術，夜過吉甫家，群即捕登掠考，上言吉甫陰事。
units.en: A man named Chen Deng, versed in divination, visited Jifu's house at night; Qun seized him, tortured him, and accused Jifu of clandestine affairs.
units.literal: Chen Deng, skilled in occult arts, passed Jifu's house by night; Qun at once arrested Deng and tortured him for confession, memorializing that Jifu had secret dealings.

units.zh: 憲宗面覆登，得其情，大怒，將誅群，吉甫為救解，乃免，出為湖南觀察使。
units.en: Xianzong examined Deng face to face, learned the facts, flew into a rage and nearly put Qun to death; Jifu interceded, he was spared, and was demoted to observation commissioner of Hunan.
units.literal: Xianzong confronted Deng in person, learned the truth, was greatly enraged, and was about to execute Qun; Jifu pleaded for him and he was spared, being sent out as Hunan observation commissioner.

units.zh: 改黔中。
units.en: His post was changed to Qianzhong.
units.literal: He was reassigned to Qianzhong.

units.zh: 會水壞城郛，調溪洞群蠻築作，因是群蠻亂，貶開州刺史。
units.en: Floods ruined the ramparts; he drafted the stream-dwelling tribes for repair work, the tribes rose in disorder, and he was demoted to prefect of Kai.
units.literal: When floods destroyed the walls, he levied the tribal peoples of the streams and caves for construction labor; on that account the tribes rebelled, and he was demoted to prefect of Kai.

units.zh: 稍遷容管經略使。
units.en: He was later transferred to military commissioner of Rongguan.
units.literal: He was gradually moved to military commissioner of Rongguan.

units.zh: 召還，卒於行，年五十五，贈左散騎常侍。
units.en: Summoned back, he died on the road at fifty-five and was posthumously made Left Regular Cavalryman-in-Attendance.
units.literal: Recalled to court, he died on the journey at age fifty-five; he was posthumously given the title of Left Regular Cavalryman-in-Attendance.

units.zh: 群狠自用，果於復怨。
units.en: Qun was harsh, willful, and swift to settle scores.
units.literal: Qun was fierce and self-willed, and ruthless in repaying grudges.

units.zh: 始召，將大任之，眾皆懼，及聞其死，乃安。
units.en: At first his recall promised high appointment and everyone feared him; when he died, the court breathed easier.
units.literal: When he was first summoned, the court was about to entrust him with great office and all were afraid; when word came of his death, people were relieved.

units.zh: 兄常、牟，弟庠、鞏，皆為郎，工詞章，為《聯珠集》行於時，義取昆弟若五星然。
units.en: Elder brothers Chang and Mou and younger brothers Ku and Gong all held gentleman posts, were skilled writers, and issued the Linked Pearls, comparing the brothers to five stars.
units.literal: His elder brothers Chang and Mou and younger brothers Ku and Gong all served as court gentlemen, excelled in belles-lettres, and compiled the Linked Pearls, which circulated in their day—the title likening the brothers to five stars.

units.zh: 常，字中行，大歷中及進士第，不肯調，客廣陵，多所論著，隱居二十年。
units.en: Chang, style name Zhongxing, took the jinshi under Dali, declined office, stayed at Guangling writing, and remained in retirement twenty years.
units.literal: Chang, styled Zhongxing, passed the jinshi in the Dali era, refused appointment, lodged at Guangling, wrote extensively, and lived in seclusion twenty years.

units.zh: 鎮州王武俊聞其才，奏辟不應。
units.en: Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou, hearing of his gifts, invited him to his staff, but Chang would not come.
units.literal: Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou, hearing of his talent, memorialized to recruit him, but he did not respond.

units.zh: 杜佑鎮淮南，署為參謀。
units.en: Du You, as Huainan commissioner, made him a staff planner.
units.literal: When Du You governed Huainan, he appointed him staff planner.

units.zh: 歷朗夔江撫四州刺史、國子祭酒，致仕。
units.en: He held prefectures of Lang, Kui, Jiang, and Fu, became Director of the Directorate of Education, and retired.
units.literal: He served successively as prefect of Lang, Kui, Jiang, and Fu and as Director of the Directorate of Education, then retired.

units.zh: 卒，贈越州都督。
units.en: After death he was posthumously made Governor-General of Yue.
units.literal: On death he was posthumously made Governor-General of Yue.

units.zh: 牟，字貽周，累佐節度府。
units.en: Mou, style name Yizhou, served many times on frontier staffs.
units.literal: Mou, styled Yizhou, repeatedly served on military commissioners' staffs.

units.zh: 晚從昭義盧從史，從史浸驕，牟度不可諫，即移疾歸東都。
units.en: In later years he followed Lu Congshi of Zhaoyi; when Congshi grew insolent, Mou saw counsel would fail, feigned illness, and returned to Luoyang.
units.literal: Late in life he followed Lu Congshi of Zhaoyi; as Congshi grew arrogant, Mou judged that he could not be admonished and pleaded illness to return to the eastern capital.

units.zh: 從史敗，不以覺微避去自賢。
units.en: When Congshi fell, Mou did not parade his early withdrawal as wisdom.
units.literal: When Congshi was defeated, he did not claim credit for having sensed trouble and withdrawn.

units.zh: 位國子司業。
units.en: He rose to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
units.literal: He reached the post of Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

units.zh: 庠，字胄卿，終婺州刺史。
units.en: Ku, style name Zhouqing, died as prefect of Wuzhou.
units.literal: Ku, styled Zhouqing, ended as prefect of Wuzhou.

units.zh: 鞏，字友封，雅裕，有名於時。
units.en: Gong, style name Youfeng, was cultivated and openhanded and enjoyed renown.
units.literal: Gong, styled Youfeng, was refined and generous and famed in his time.

units.zh: 平居與人言若不出口，世號「囁嚅翁」。
units.en: In daily talk he seemed barely to open his mouth; contemporaries dubbed him "the Muttering Old Man."
units.literal: In ordinary conversation with others he seemed scarcely to speak; the age called him "the Muttering Old Man."

units.zh: 元稹節度武昌，奏鞏自副，卒。
units.en: Yuan Zhen, commissioner at Wuchang, had Gong appointed his aide; Gong died in that post.
units.literal: When Yuan Zhen was military commissioner at Wuchang, he memorialized for Gong as his deputy; Gong died in office.

units.zh: 劉棲楚，其出寒鄙。
units.en: Liu Qichu sprang from poor and low birth.
units.literal: Liu Qichu came from humble and mean origins.

units.zh: 為鎮州小吏，王承宗奇之，薦於李逢吉，繇鄧州司倉參軍擢右拾遺。
units.en: A minor clerk in Zhenzhou, he won Wang Chengzong's notice, was recommended to Li Fengji, and rose from Dengzhou warehouse aide to Right Reminder.
units.literal: He was a petty clerk in Zhenzhou; Wang Chengzong admired him and recommended him to Li Fengji, by whom he was raised from Dengzhou warehouse aide to Right Reminder.

units.zh: 逢吉之罷裴度、逐李紳，皆嗾而為奸者。
units.en: Fengji's ouster of Pei Du and banishment of Li Shen were both driven by Qichu as his scheming henchman.
units.literal: Fengji's dismissal of Pei Du and expulsion of Li Shen were both urged on by Qichu as his crafty accomplice.

units.zh: 敬宗立，視朝常晏，數遊畋失德。
units.en: Under Jingzong, audiences were habitually late and the emperor often hunted to the neglect of rule.
units.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he was tardy at morning audience and often went hunting in neglect of duty.

units.zh: 棲楚諫曰：「惟前世王者初嗣位，皆親庶政，坐以待旦。
units.en: Qichu admonished: "Ancient kings at the start of their reigns personally handled government, sitting up to await dawn.
units.literal: Qichu remonstrated: "Former sage-kings at the beginning of their reigns all personally attended to common affairs, sitting to await the dawn.

units.zh: 陛下新即位，安臥寢內，日晏乃作。
units.en: Yet Your Majesty, newly enthroned, rests in the inner quarters and does not rise until late morning.
units.literal: Your Majesty has newly taken the throne yet lies at ease within the inner apartments, not rising until the sun is high.

units.zh: 大行殯宮密邇，鼓吹之聲日聞諸朝。
units.en: The late emperor's mourning hall is near, and dirges daily resound through the palace.
units.literal: The late emperor's coffin hall is close by, and the sound of funeral music daily reaches the court.

units.zh: 且憲宗及先帝皆長君，朝夕恪勤，四方猶有叛者。
units.en: Xianzong and the previous emperor were seasoned rulers who labored dawn to dusk, yet rebels still rose on every side.
units.literal: Moreover, both Emperor Xianzong and the prior emperor were mature rulers who toiled diligently morning and evening, yet rebellion still arose in the four quarters.

units.zh: 陛下以少主，踐祚未幾，惡德流布，恐福祚之不長也。
units.en: Your Majesty is a young ruler newly enthroned; bad conduct is already rumored—I fear your blessing will not last.
units.literal: Your Majesty is a young sovereign who has barely ascended; ill repute spreads abroad—I fear your fortune will not long endure.

units.zh: 臣以諫為官，使陛下負天下譏，請碎首以謝。」
units.en: As remonstrator, if Your Majesty earns the empire's censure, I ask to dash out my brains in atonement."
units.literal: I hold the office of remonstrator; if Your Majesty bears the world's reproach, I beg to dash my head and atone."

units.zh: 遂額叩龍墀，血被面。
units.en: He then beat his brow on the dragon pavement until his face ran with blood.
units.literal: He then struck his forehead on the imperial steps until blood covered his face.

units.zh: 李逢吉傳詔：「毋叩頭，待詔旨。」
units.en: Fengji relayed the decree: "Cease knocking your head; await the throne's word."
units.literal: Li Fengji transmitted the edict: "Do not knock your head; await the imperial command."

units.zh: 棲楚捧首立，帝動容，揚袂使去。
units.en: Qichu stood clutching his head; the emperor was stirred, gestured dismissal, and had him led away.
units.literal: Qichu held his head and stood; the emperor was moved, waved his sleeve, and had him withdraw.

units.zh: 棲楚曰：「不聽臣言，臣請死於此。」
units.en: Qichu said, "If you will not hear me, I beg to die on this spot."
units.literal: Qichu said, "If Your Majesty will not heed my words, I ask to die here."

units.zh: 有詔尉諭，乃出。
units.en: An edict soothed him, and only then did he withdraw.
units.literal: An edict comforted him, and he then left.

units.zh: 遷起居郎，辭疾歸洛。
units.en: He became Diarist, pleaded illness, and retired to Luoyang.
units.literal: He was promoted to Diarist, then resigned on grounds of illness and returned to Luoyang.

units.zh: 後諫官對延英，帝問：「向廷爭者在邪？」
units.en: Later, when remonstrators met the emperor at Yanying, he asked, "Is the one who quarreled in court here?"
units.literal: Later, when remonstrators faced the emperor in the Yanying Hall, the emperor asked, "Is the man who disputed in court present?"

units.zh: 以諫議大夫召。
units.en: He was recalled as Remonstrator of the Left.
units.literal: He was summoned as Remonstrator of the Left.

units.zh: 未幾，宣授刑部侍郎。
units.en: Soon he received direct appointment as Vice Minister of Justice.
units.literal: Before long he was directly appointed Vice Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 故事，侍郎無宣授者，逢吉喜助己，故不次任之。
units.en: By precedent vice ministers were not directly commissioned; Fengji, glad of his support, broke precedent to elevate him.
units.literal: By precedent vice ministers were not directly appointed; Fengji was pleased that he aided him, and so gave him this extraordinary post.

units.zh: 數月，改京兆尹，峻誅罰，不避權豪。
units.en: Months later he became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, harsh in penalties and fearless of magnates.
units.literal: After several months he was made metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, severe in punishment and unafraid of the powerful.

units.zh: 先是，諸惡少竄名北軍，淩藉衣冠，有罪則逃軍中，無敢捕。
units.en: Hoodlums had hidden in the northern armies, insulting the gentry; on crime they fled to the camps and none dared seize them.
units.literal: Before this, vicious youths had enrolled in the northern armies, bullying the gentry; when guilty they fled into the army and none dared arrest them.

units.zh: 棲楚一切窮治，不閱旬，宿奸老蠹為斂跡。
units.en: Qichu pursued every case to the limit; within ten days old evils drew in their claws.
units.literal: Qichu prosecuted them all to the end; within ten days the entrenched villains shrank back.

units.zh: 一日，軍士乘醉有所淩突，諸少年從旁噪曰：「癡男子，不記頭上尹邪？」
units.en: Once a drunken soldier caused a disturbance; youths nearby yelled, "Idiot—have you forgotten the magistrate above your head?"
units.literal: One day a soldier, drunk, committed some outrage; the youths nearby shouted, "Fool—don't you remember the magistrate on your head?"

units.zh: 然其性詭激，敢為怪行，乘險抵巇，若無顧藉，內實恃權怙寵以幹進。
units.en: Yet he was perverse and rash, performing shocking stunts and courting danger as if fearless, while inwardly he leaned on patronage to claw upward.
units.literal: Yet his nature was devious and impulsive; he dared strange acts, courting peril on sheer cliffs as if he had nothing to lose, while inwardly he relied on power and favor to force advancement.

units.zh: 詣宰相，厲色慢辭，韋處厚惡之，出為桂管觀察使。
units.en: At the chancellors' offices he glared and spoke rudely; Wei Chuhou loathed him and posted him to Guiguan as observation commissioner.
units.literal: Visiting the chief ministers, he spoke with fierce looks and insolent words; Wei Chuhou detested him and sent him out as Guiguan observation commissioner.

units.zh: 卒，贈左散騎常侍。
units.en: He died and was posthumously given Left Regular Cavalryman-in-Attendance.
units.literal: He died and was posthumously made Left Regular Cavalryman-in-Attendance.

units.zh: 張又新，字孔昭，工部侍郎薦之子。
units.en: Zhang Youxin, style name Kongzhao, was the son of Vice Minister of Works Zhang Jian.
units.literal: Zhang Youxin, styled Kongzhao, was son of Vice Minister of Works Zhang Jian.

units.zh: 元和中，及進士高第，歷左右補闕。
units.en: In Yuanhe he placed high on the jinshi and served as Left and Right Supplementation Officer.
units.literal: In the Yuanhe era he took high honors in the jinshi examination and served as Left and Right Supplementation Officer.

units.zh: 性傾邪。
units.en: He was by nature devious.
units.literal: His nature was crooked.

units.zh: 李逢吉用事，惡李紳，冀得其罪，求中朝兇果敢言者厚之，以危中紳。
units.en: Fengji, hating Li Shen, sought grounds against him, found bold speakers at court, and richly paid them to imperil Shen.
units.literal: Li Fengji held power, hated Li Shen, and hoped to find crime in him; he sought fierce and bold men at court who dared speak and richly rewarded them to endanger Shen.

units.zh: 又新與拾遺李續、劉棲楚等為逢吉搏吠所憎，故有「八關十六子」之目。
units.en: Youxin, with Li Xu and Liu Qichu, were detested as Fengji's attack dogs, earning the name "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."
units.literal: Youxin, with Reminder Li Xu and Liu Qichu, were Fengji's attack dogs and were hated for it, hence the label "Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."

units.zh: 敬宗立，紳貶端州司馬，朝臣過宰相賀，閽者曰：「止，宰相方與補闕語，姑伺之。」
units.en: At Jingzong's accession Shen was demoted to Duanzhou Sima; officials coming to congratulate the chancellor were told, "Wait—the chancellor is with the Supplementation Officer."
units.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, Shen was demoted to Sima of Duanzhou; as courtiers passed the chancellor to congratulate, the doorkeeper said, "Stop—the chancellor is speaking with the Supplementation Officer; wait a moment."

units.zh: 及又新出，流汗揖百官曰：「端溪之事，竊不敢讓。」
units.en: When Youxin emerged, drenched in sweat, he bowed to the officials: "The Duanxi affair—I dare not deny my part."
units.literal: When Youxin came out, sweating, he bowed to the officials and said, "As for the affair at Duanxi, I dare not disclaim credit."

units.zh: 人皆辟易畏之。
units.en: Everyone recoiled in dread.
units.literal: All shrank back in fear of him.

units.zh: 尋轉祠部員外郎。
units.en: He was soon made Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

units.zh: 嘗買婢遷約，為牙儈搜索陵突，御史劾舉，逢吉庇之，事不窮治。
units.en: He once bought a maidservant then reneged; the broker searched and humiliated him; censors impeached him, but Fengji protected him and the matter was not pressed.
units.literal: Once, buying a slave girl, he broke the contract; the broker searched and insulted him; the censorate impeached him, but Fengji shielded him and the case was not fully pursued.

units.zh: 及逢吉罷，領山南東道節度，表又新為行軍司馬。
units.en: When Fengji lost office and went to the Shannan East Circuit, he took Youxin as campaign Sima.
units.literal: When Fengji fell from power and took the Shannan East Circuit command, he had Youxin as his campaign staff Sima.

units.zh: 坐田伾事，貶汀州刺史。
units.en: Implicated in Tian Pi's case, he was demoted to prefect of Ting.
units.literal: For involvement in Tian Pi's affair he was demoted to prefect of Ting.

units.zh: 李訓有寵，又新復見用，遷刑部郎中，為申州刺史。
units.en: When Li Xun rose, Youxin was restored, made Director of Justice, and sent to Shen as prefect.
units.literal: When Li Xun gained favor, Youxin was again employed, made Director in the Ministry of Justice, and sent as prefect of Shen.

units.zh: 訓死，復坐貶。
units.en: After Xun's death he was demoted again.
units.literal: When Xun died, he was again demoted for guilt.

units.zh: 終左司郎中。
units.en: He finished as Left Department Director.
units.literal: He ended as Left Department Director.

units.zh: 又新善文辭，再以諂附敗，喪其家聲雲。
units.en: Youxin wrote well yet twice destroyed his house's reputation by fawning on power.
units.literal: Youxin was skilled in letters but twice ruined his family name through flattery and attachment.

units.zh: 楊虞卿，字師臯，虢州弘農人。
units.en: Yang Yuqing, style name Shigao, came from Hongnong in Guo.
units.literal: Yang Yuqing, styled Shigao, was a native of Hongnong in Guo Prefecture.

units.zh: 父寧，有高操，談辯可喜。
units.en: His father Ning was high-minded, eloquent, and engaging in discourse.
units.literal: His father Ning possessed lofty integrity and was pleasant in debate and eloquence.

units.zh: 擢明經，調臨渙主簿，棄官還夏，與陽城為莫逆交。
units.en: Ning passed the Mingjing, served as Linhuan chief clerk, quit office, returned home to Xia, and became Yang Cheng's closest friend.
units.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination, was appointed chief clerk of Linhuan, resigned, returned to Xia, and became sworn friend with Yang Cheng.

units.zh: 德宗以諫議大夫召城，城未拜，詔寧即諭，與俱來。
units.en: Dezong summoned Cheng as Left Remonstrator; before Cheng accepted, the throne ordered Ning to urge him, and both arrived.
units.literal: Dezong summoned Cheng as Remonstrator of the Left; Cheng had not yet accepted; the emperor ordered Ning at once to persuade him, and they came together.

units.zh: 陜虢觀察使李齊運表置幕府。
units.en: Observation commissioner Li Qiyun of Shan-Guo placed him on staff.
units.literal: Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of Shan-Guo, memorialized to place him on his staff.

units.zh: 齊運入為京兆尹，表奉先主簿，拜監察御史，坐累免。
units.en: When Qiyun became Jingzhao magistrate, he recommended Ning as Fengxian chief clerk; Ning became Attending Censor but was dismissed for a fault.
units.literal: When Qiyun became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, he recommended him as chief clerk of Fengxian; he was made Attending Censor and dismissed for an offense.

units.zh: 順宗初，召為殿中侍御史，終國子祭酒。
units.en: Early in Shunzong's reign he was recalled as Palace Attending Censor and died as Director of Education.
units.literal: At the beginning of Shunzong's reign he was summoned as Attending Censor within the Palace and died as Director of the Directorate of Education.

units.zh: 虞卿第進士、博學宏辭，為校書郎。
units.en: Yuqing took jinshi and erudite macrocosmic degrees and served as collator.
units.literal: Yuqing passed the jinshi and the erudite macrocosmic examination and served as collator.

units.zh: 抵淮南，委婚幣焉，會陳商葬其先，貧不振，虞卿未嘗與遊，悉所賫助之。
units.en: Bound for Huainan with betrothal gifts, he found Chen Shang burying his ancestors too poor to proceed; though strangers, Yuqing gave all he had to aid him.
units.literal: Going to Huainan, he entrusted betrothal gifts; Chen Shang was burying his forebears and was too poor to manage it—Yuqing had never associated with him yet gave all he carried to help.

units.zh: 擢累監察御史。
units.en: He rose through successive appointments as Attending Censor.
units.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Attending Censor.

units.zh: 穆宗初立，逸遊荒恣，虞卿上疏曰：「烏鳶遭害仁鳥逝，誹謗不誅良臣進。
units.en: At Muzong's accession, given to idle roaming and dissipation, Yuqing submitted: "When carrion birds are harmed, the virtuous birds flee; when calumny goes unpunished, good ministers come forward.
units.literal: When Emperor Muzong first took the throne, indulging in roaming pleasures and reckless abandon, Yuqing memorialized: "When crows and kites suffer harm the benevolent birds depart; when slander is not punished worthy ministers advance.

units.zh: 臣敢冒誅獻瞽言。
units.en: I dare risk death to offer my humble counsel.
units.literal: Your servant dares risk execution to offer blind counsel.

units.zh: 臣聞堯、舜以天下為憂，不以位為樂。
units.en: I have heard that Yao and Shun worried for the realm rather than rejoiced in their rank.
units.literal: Your servant has heard that Yao and Shun took the empire's cares as their own and did not treat the throne as pleasure.

units.zh: 況今北虜方梗，西戎弗靖，兩河有瘡痏之虞，五嶺罹氛厲之役。
units.en: The northern enemy blocks the frontier, the western tribes are unquiet, the two He circuits bear festering troubles, and the Five Ridges labor under plague and levy.
units.literal: Moreover, the northern barbarians are now obstructive, the western tribes unsettled, the two He regions face the peril of running sores, and the Five Ridges suffer pestilence and corvée.

units.zh: 人之疾苦積下，朝之制度莫脩。
units.en: Popular hardship piles up below, yet court institutions go unmended.
units.literal: The people's suffering accumulates below, while the court's institutions are not repaired.

units.zh: 邊亡見儲，國用浸屈，固未可以高枕而息也。
units.en: Border granaries stand empty and the treasury shrinks; one cannot pillow one's head high and sleep in peace.
units.literal: The borders show empty stores, state revenue daily contracts—truly one cannot rest high on a pillow and be at ease.

units.zh: 陛下初臨萬幾，宜有憂天下心。
units.en: Your Majesty has only just taken the myriad reins; you should bear the empire in mind.
units.literal: Your Majesty has newly assumed the myriad affairs; you ought to have a heart that worries for the empire.

units.zh: 當日見輔臣公卿百執事，垂意以問，使四方內外灼有所聞。
units.en: Meet your chief ministers, nobles, and the hundred officers daily, question them with care, and let the realm see it plainly.
units.literal: Each day you should receive chief ministers, dukes, and the hundred officials, showing concern in inquiry, so that within and without all clearly hear.

units.zh: 而聽政六十日，入對延英，獨三數大臣承聖問而已，它內朝臣偕入齊出，無所咨詢。
units.en: Yet in sixty days at court, at Yanying audiences only a few senior ministers heard your questions; the rest of the inner officials filed in and out with no counsel sought.
units.literal: Yet in sixty days of hearing government, entering audience at Yanying, only three or four great ministers received the sacred inquiry; other inner-court officials entered and left together with no consultation.

units.zh: 諫臣盈廷，忠言不聞，臣實羞之。
units.en: The remonstrators crowd the hall yet loyal speech never reaches you—I am ashamed of it.
units.literal: Remonstrators fill the hall yet loyal words are not heard—I am truly ashamed.

units.zh: 蓋主恩疏而正路塞也。
units.en: Imperial grace has grown remote and the straight road is blocked.
units.literal: This is because imperial favor is distant and the upright path blocked.

units.zh: 公卿大臣宜朝夕燕見，則君臣情接而治道得矣。
units.en: High ministers should meet you morning and evening in relaxed audience, so feeling joins between ruler and servant and governance is secured.
units.literal: Dukes and great ministers ought to be received morning and evening in easy audience, so that ruler and minister join in feeling and the way of rule is attained.

units.zh: 今宰臣四五人，或頃刻侍坐，鞠躬隕越，隨旨上下，無能往來，此繇君太尊、臣太卑故也。
units.en: Today four or five chancellors may sit a moment, bowing until they nearly fall, bobbing at your nod, unable to speak freely—because the throne is too lofty and the servants too abject.
units.literal: Now four or five chief ministers sometimes sit for a moment, bowing with bodies bent low, rising and falling at the imperial will, unable to exchange words—this is because the lord is too exalted and the servants too low.

units.zh: 公卿列位，雖陟降清地，曾未奉優眷、承下問。
units.en: The ranked nobles, though raised to exalted posts, have never tasted your gracious notice or your questioning ear.
units.literal: The ranks of dukes, though promoted to pure posts, have never received gracious favor or answered inquiry from below.

units.zh: 雖陛下神聖如五帝，猶宜周爰顧逮，惠以氣色，使支體相成，君臣昭明。
units.en: Even if you are as sage as the Five Emperors, you should still look widely, show a warm face, and knit trunk and limbs so ruler and minister shine upon each other.
units.literal: Though Your Majesty is as sagely as the Five Emperors, you should still look about with care, show a kindly countenance, and make limbs and trunk work together so ruler and minister are bright to each other.

units.zh: 陛下求治於宰相，宰相求治於臣等，進忠若趨利，論政若訴冤，此而不治，無有也。
units.en: You seek order from the chancellor, the chancellor from us; if loyalty is pursued like profit and policy debated like a grievance, nothing will remain ungoverned.
units.literal: Your Majesty seeks good rule from the chancellor; the chancellor seeks good rule from us; if advancing loyalty is like rushing profit and discussing government like pleading wrongs, with this there will be no failure to govern.

units.zh: 自古天子居危思安之心同，而居安慮危之心則異，故不得皆為聖明也。」
units.en: In danger all rulers think of safety alike, but in safety their thoughts of peril differ—so not every throne is sage."
units.literal: From antiquity the hearts of sons of Heaven in peril thinking of safety are the same, but in safety thinking of peril they differ—hence not all can be sage and bright."

units.zh: 時又有衡山布衣趙知微，亦上書指言帝倡優在側，馳騁無度，內作色荒，外作禽荒。
units.en: Meanwhile Zhao Zhiwei, a Hengshan commoner, also wrote, accusing the emperor of keeping entertainers at hand, hunting without restraint, indulging lust within and sport without.
units.literal: At the time the commoner Zhao Zhiwei of Hengshan also memorialized, pointing out that the emperor kept actors at his side, rode and hunted without limit, made inner lewdness and outer bird-chasing excess.

units.zh: 辭頗危切，帝詔宰相尉謝。
units.en: His language was severe; the emperor had the chancellor console and thank him.
units.literal: His words were very sharp; the emperor ordered the chancellor to comfort and thank him.

units.zh: 宰相因是賀天子納諫，然不能用也。
units.en: The chancellor then congratulated the throne on heeding criticism, but nothing was acted upon.
units.literal: The chancellor therefore congratulated Heaven's Son on accepting remonstrance, yet the advice could not be used.

units.zh: 俄詔行勞西北邊。
units.en: Soon he was ordered to tour and comfort the northwest border.
units.literal: Soon an edict sent him to comfort the northwest frontier.

units.zh: 還，遷侍御史，改禮部員外郎、史館脩撰。
units.en: Returning, he became Attending Censor, then Vice Director of Rites and Historiography compiler.
units.literal: On return he was made Attending Censor, then Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

units.zh: 進吏部。
units.en: He rose to the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: He advanced to the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 會曹史李賨等鬻偽告，調官六十五員，贓千六百萬以上，虞卿發其奸，賨等系御史府。
units.en: Clerks led by Li Bin sold forged appointment notices for sixty-five posts, taking more than sixteen million in bribes; Yuqing exposed them and they were jailed in the censorate.
units.literal: When clerks Li Bin and others sold false appointment notices, adjusting sixty-five offices, with bribes above sixteen million, Yuqing exposed the fraud and Bin and the rest were held in the censorate prison.

units.zh: 而虞卿親吏嘗受二百萬，亡命，私奴受三十萬，虞卿縛奴送獄。
units.en: His own clerk had taken two million and fled; a household slave took three hundred thousand—Yuqing tied the slave and sent him to jail.
units.literal: Yet Yuqing's personal clerk had once taken two million and fled; a private slave took three hundred thousand—Yuqing bound the slave and sent him to prison.

units.zh: 三司嚴休復、高鉞、韋景休雜推，賨等皆誅死。
units.en: The Three Offices, Yan Xiufu, Gao Qian, and Wei Jingxiu, jointly judged them; Bin and his fellows were all put to death.
units.literal: The Three Offices—Yan Xiufu, Gao Qian, and Wei Jingxiu—jointly tried the case; Bin and the rest were all executed.

units.zh: 虞卿坐不檢下免官。
units.en: Yuqing lost office for failing to discipline his staff.
units.literal: Yuqing was dismissed for not restraining subordinates.

units.zh: 李宗閔、牛僧孺輔政，引為右司郎中、弘文館學士。
units.en: Under Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru he became Right Department Director and Hongwen academician.
units.literal: When Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru held government, they brought him in as Right Department Director and Erudite of the Hongwen Institute.

units.zh: 再遷給事中。
units.en: He was promoted again to Supervising Censor.
units.literal: He was again promoted to Supervising Censor.

units.zh: 虞卿佞柔，善諧麗權幸，倚為奸利。
units.en: Yuqing was pliant and flattering, adept at charming favorites, and traded on them for corrupt profit.
units.literal: Yuqing was fawning and supple, skilled at pleasing the powerful with witty grace, relying on them for illicit gain.

units.zh: 歲舉選者，皆走門下，署第註員，無不得所欲，升沈在牙頰間。
units.en: Annual candidates thronged his door; he marked ranks and posts, and none missed his favor—advancement or ruin hung on his word.
units.literal: Each year those seeking selection all ran to his gate; he annotated ranks and posts, and none failed to get what they wished—promotion and demotion lay on the tip of his tongue.

units.zh: 當時有蘇景胤、張元夫，而虞卿兄弟汝士、漢公為人所奔向，故語曰：「欲趨舉場，問蘇、張；
units.en: Su Jingyin and Zhang Yuanfu still mattered, but Yuqing's brothers Rushi and Hangong drew the crowds, so people said: "For the examination field, ask Su and Zhang;
units.literal: At the time there were Su Jingyin and Zhang Yuanfu, but Yuqing's brothers Rushi and Hangong were where men rushed, hence the saying: "If you wish to hurry to the examination ground, ask Su and Zhang;

units.zh: 蘇、張猶可，三楊殺我。」
units.en: Su and Zhang may suffice—the three Yangs will ruin you."
units.literal: Su and Zhang are still tolerable—the three Yangs will kill me."

units.zh: 宗閔待之尤厚，就黨中為最能唱和者，以口語軒輊事機，故時號「黨魁」。
units.en: Zongmin favored him most; in the clique he led the chorus and steered affairs by rumor, earning the title "Faction Chief."
units.literal: Zongmin treated him especially well; among the faction he was the best at echoing and harmonizing, weighing affairs by gossip, hence the nickname "Faction Chief."

units.zh: 德裕之相，出為常州刺史。
units.en: When Deyu took the chancellorship, Yuqing was posted to Changzhou as prefect.
units.literal: When Deyu became chancellor, Yuqing was sent out as prefect of Chang.

units.zh: 宗閔復入，以工部侍郎召，遷京兆尹。
units.en: Zongmin's return brought him back as Vice Minister of Works and Jingzhao magistrate.
units.literal: When Zongmin returned to power, he was summoned as Vice Minister of Works and made metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 太和九年，京師訛言鄭註為帝治丹，剔小兒肝心用之。
units.en: In Taihe year nine the capital rumored that Zheng Zhu brewed elixir for the emperor by cutting out children's livers and hearts.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe, the capital rumor said Zheng Zhu was making elixir for the emperor, gouging out small boys' livers and hearts for use.

units.zh: 民相驚，扃護兒曹。
units.en: Families panicked and locked their children in.
units.literal: The people were alarmed and barred their children indoors.

units.zh: 帝不悅，註亦內不安，而雅與虞卿有怨，即約李訓奏言：「語出虞卿家，因京兆騶伍布都下。」
units.en: The emperor was angered; Zhu, ill at ease and hostile to Yuqing, with Li Xun claimed: "The tale began in Yuqing's household and was spread by Jingzhao runners throughout the capital."
units.literal: The emperor was displeased; Zhu was uneasy within, and having long hated Yuqing, joined Li Xun in memorializing: "The talk came from Yuqing's house and was spread through the city by the Jingzhao courier runners."

units.zh: 御史大夫李固言素嫉虞卿周比，因傅左端倪。
units.en: Censor-in-chief Li Guyan, who loathed Yuqing's faction ties, seized on loose ends.
units.literal: Censor-in-chief Li Guyan had long detested Yuqing's cliquishness and seized on slight signs.

units.zh: 帝大怒，下虞卿詔獄。
units.en: The emperor flew into a rage and imprisoned Yuqing.
units.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and sent Yuqing to the imperial prison.

units.zh: 於是諸子弟自囚闕下稱冤，虞卿得釋，貶虔州司戶參軍，死。
units.en: His sons and brothers then chained themselves at the palace gate pleading injustice; he was freed, demoted to Qianzhou army aide, and died.
units.literal: Then the sons and brothers imprisoned themselves below the palace gate crying injustice; Yuqing was released, demoted to Qianzhou army aide, and died.

units.zh: 子知退、知權、壇、堪、漢公，皆擢進士第，漢公最顯。
units.en: Sons Zhitui, Zhiquan, Tan, Kan, and Hangong all took the jinshi; Hangong shone brightest.
units.literal: Sons Zhituo, Zhiquan, Tan, Kan, and Hangong all passed the jinshi; Hangong was most prominent.

units.zh: 漢公，字用乂。
units.en: Hangong, style name Yongyi.
units.literal: Hangong, styled Yongyi.

units.zh: 始辟興元李絳幕府，絳死，不與其禍。
units.en: He began on Li Jiang's Xingyuan staff; when Jiang perished, he escaped the purge.
units.literal: He first entered the staff of Li Jiang of Xingyuan; when Jiang died, he did not share in the calamity.

units.zh: 遷累戶部郎中、史館修撰，轉司封郎中。
units.en: He advanced from Revenue Director and Historiography compiler to Rites Director.
units.literal: He rose through Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Historiography compiler to Director in the Ministry of Rites.

units.zh: 坐虞卿，下除舒州刺史，徙湖、亳、蘇三州。
units.en: Implicated through Yuqing, he was demoted to Shu prefect, then served Hu, Bo, and Su.
units.literal: For Yuqing's guilt he was demoted to prefect of Shu, then moved through Hu, Bo, and Su.

units.zh: 擢桂管、浙東觀察使。
units.en: He became observation commissioner of Guiguan and Zhedong.
units.literal: He was raised to observation commissioner of Guiguan and Zhedong.

units.zh: 繇戶部侍郎拜荊南節度使，召為工部尚書。
units.en: From Revenue Vice Minister he was made Jingnan military commissioner, then recalled as Minister of Works.
units.literal: From Vice Minister of Revenue he was made military commissioner of Jingnan and summoned as Minister of Works.

units.zh: 或劾漢公治荊南有貪贓，降秘書監。
units.en: Accused of graft in Jingnan, he was demoted to Secretariat Director.
units.literal: Some impeached him for corruption governing Jingnan, and he was reduced to Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 稍遷國子祭酒。
units.en: He was later made Director of Education.
units.literal: He was gradually moved to Director of the Directorate of Education.

units.zh: 宣宗擢為同州刺史。
units.en: Emperor Xuanzong appointed him prefect of Tong.
units.literal: Emperor Xuanzong promoted him to prefect of Tong.

units.zh: 於是，給事中鄭裔綽、鄭公輿共奏漢公冒猥無廉概，不可處近輔，三還制書。
units.en: Supervising Censors Zheng Yichuo and Zheng Gongyu then wrote that Hangong was brazen and corrupt, unfit for the inner court, and thrice returned the appointment edict.
units.literal: Then Supervising Censors Zheng Yichuo and Zheng Gongyu jointly memorialized that Hangong was shameless and without integrity, unfit for close service, and three times returned the edict.

units.zh: 帝它日凡門下論執駁正未嘗卻。
units.en: On ordinary days the throne never overruled Secretariat objections.
units.literal: On other days whenever the Secretariat debated and rejected, the emperor never overruled.

units.zh: 漢公素結左右，有奧助。
units.en: Hangong had long cultivated palace eunuchs who backed him in secret.
units.literal: Hangong had long cultivated the inner attendants and had hidden backers.

units.zh: 至是，帝惑不從，制卒行。
units.en: Now the emperor wavered and ignored them; the appointment stood.
units.literal: This time the emperor was swayed and did not heed them; the edict was finally issued.

units.zh: 會寒食宴近臣，帝自擊球為樂，巡勞從臣，見裔綽等曰：「省中議無不從，唯漢公事為有黨。」
units.en: At a Cold Food feast he played ball himself, greeted his intimates, and told Yichuo and the others: "You never oppose me except over Hangong—that is faction."
units.literal: At a Cold Food feast for close ministers the emperor himself played ball for sport, touring to comfort his followers, and seeing Yichuo and the rest said: "The Secretariat has never refused my word except on Hangong's affair—there is faction at work."

units.zh: 裔綽獨對：「同州，太宗興王地。
units.en: Yichuo alone answered: "Tong was where Taizong began his kingship.
units.literal: Yichuo alone replied: "Tongzhou is the land where Taizong rose as king.

units.zh: 陛下為人子孫當精擇守長付之，漢公既以墨敗，陛下容可舉劇部私貪人？」
units.en: As his descendant you should choose governors carefully; Hangong is already stained by ink—can you give a major post to a known grafter for favor?"
units.literal: Your Majesty, as descendant, ought to choose governors with care; Hangong has already failed for corruption—can Your Majesty appoint a greedy man to a great post for private reasons?"

units.zh: 帝恚見顏間。
units.en: Anger flickered on the emperor's face.
units.literal: The emperor's anger showed on his face.

units.zh: 翌日，斥裔綽為商州刺史。
units.en: Next day Yichuo was sent out as Shang prefect.
units.literal: The next day Yichuo was demoted to prefect of Shang.

units.zh: 漢公自同州更宣武、天平兩節度使，卒。
units.en: Hangong went from Tong to Xuanwu and Tianping as military commissioner and died.
units.literal: Hangong moved from Tong to the two commands of Xuanwu and Tianping and died.

units.zh: 子籌、範，仕亦顯。
units.en: Sons Chou and Fan likewise achieved distinction.
units.literal: Sons Chou and Fan also rose to prominence.

units.zh: 汝士，字慕巢。
units.en: Rushi, style name Muchao.
units.literal: Rushi, styled Muchao.

units.zh: 中進士第，又擢宏辭。
units.en: He took the jinshi and also the erudite macrocosmic degree.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi and also won the erudite macrocosmic examination.

units.zh: 牛李待之善，引為中書舍人。
units.en: The Niu-Li factions favored him and made him Secretariat Drafter.
units.literal: The Niu and Li factions treated him well and made him Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 開成初，繇兵部侍郎為東川節度使。
units.en: Early in Kaicheng he rose from War Vice Minister to Dongchuan military commissioner.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he went from Vice Minister of War to military commissioner of Dongchuan.

units.zh: 時嗣復鎮西川，乃族昆弟，對擁旄節，世榮其門。
units.en: Sifu then held Xichuan; as kinsmen they faced each other with banners, and the world honored their clan.
units.literal: At the time Sifu governed Xichuan—they were clan brothers, each holding a command, and the age gloried their house.

units.zh: 終刑部尚書。
units.en: He died as Minister of Justice.
units.literal: He ended as Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 子知溫、知至，悉以進士第入官。
units.en: Sons Zhiwen and Zhizhi entered service by jinshi.
units.literal: Sons Zhiwen and Zhizhi all entered office through the jinshi.

units.zh: 知溫終荊南節度使。
units.en: Zhiwen finished as Jingnan military commissioner.
units.literal: Zhiwen ended as military commissioner of Jingnan.

units.zh: 知至為宰相劉瞻所善，以比部郎中知制誥。
units.en: Zhizhi, cherished by Liu Zhan, became Drafting Drafter from Revenue Director.
units.literal: Zhizhi was favored by Chancellor Liu Zhan, made Drafting Drafter from Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 瞻得罪，亦貶瓊州司馬，擢累戶部侍郎。
units.en: When Zhan was ruined, Zhizhi was demoted to Qiongzhou Sima, then climbed again to Revenue Vice Minister.
units.literal: When Zhan fell, Zhizhi was also demoted to Sima of Qiongzhou, then gradually rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 楊氏自汝士後，貴赫為冠族。
units.en: From Rushi onward the Yangs became the foremost noble house.
units.literal: After Rushi the Yang clan became the most illustrious of great houses.

units.zh: 所居靜恭裏，兄弟並列門戟。
units.en: In Jinggong Lane the brothers each bore gate halberds.
units.literal: At their residence in Jinggong Lane the brothers each displayed gate halberds.

units.zh: 咸通後，在臺省方鎮率十餘人。
units.en: After Xiantong more than ten held capital or frontier posts.
units.literal: After Xiantong more than ten of them held posts in the central bureaus or as frontier commissioners.

units.zh: 張宿者，本寒人，自名諸生。
units.en: Zhang Su was born poor yet called himself a literatus.
units.literal: Zhang Su came from humble origins yet styled himself a scholar.

units.zh: 憲宗為廣陵王時，因張茂宗薦尉，得出入邸中，誕譎敢言。
units.en: As Prince of Guangling, Xianzong took him in through Zhang Maozong as aide; he entered the mansion, sly and outspoken.
units.literal: When Xianzong was Prince of Guangling, through Zhang Maozong's recommendation as aide he gained access to the prince's residence, crafty and bold in speech.

units.zh: 及監撫，自布衣授左拾遺，交通權幸，四方賂遺滿門。
units.en: On becoming heir apparent he rose from commoner to Left Reminder, courted favorites, and gifts from every quarter clogged his door.
units.literal: When appointed heir he was raised from common cloth to Left Reminder, trafficked with the powerful, and bribes from the four quarters filled his gate.

units.zh: 數召對，不能慎密，坐漏禁中語，貶郴丞十餘年。
units.en: Called to audience repeatedly, he could not hold his tongue and was demoted to Chen aide for over ten years for leaking inner-court words.
units.literal: Summoned to audience many times, he could not keep secrets and was demoted to Chen prefecture aide for more than ten years for leaking palace speech.

units.zh: 累遷比部員外郎。
units.en: He rose step by step to Revenue Vice Director.
units.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 宰相李逢吉數言其狡譎不可信，白為濠州刺史，宿上疏自言，留不遣。
units.en: Fengji often called him treacherous and had him sent to Hao as prefect; Su petitioned in his own defense and was kept at court.
units.literal: Chancellor Li Fengji often said he was cunning and untrustworthy and had him made prefect of Hao; Su memorialized on his own behalf and was kept from going.

units.zh: 帝欲以為諫議大夫，逢吉曰：「諫議職要重，當待賢者。
units.en: The emperor wanted him as Left Remonstrator; Fengji said: "That office is weighty and should go to a worthy man.
units.literal: The emperor wished to make him Remonstrator of the Left; Fengji said: "The remonstrator's post is weighty and should await a worthy man.

units.zh: 宿細人，不可使汙是官。
units.en: Su is a small man and must not defile it.
units.literal: Su is a petty man—he must not be allowed to stain that office.

units.zh: 陛下必用之，請先去臣乃可。」
units.en: If you insist on using him, remove me first."
units.literal: If Your Majesty must use him, please remove me first."

units.zh: 帝不悅。
units.en: The emperor took offense.
units.literal: The emperor was displeased.

units.zh: 後逢吉罷，詔權知諫議大夫，宰相崔群、王涯同請曰：「諫議大夫，前世或自山林、擢行伍任之者，然皆道義卓異於時。
units.en: After Fengji's fall an edict made Su acting Left Remonstrator; Cui Qun and Wang Ya petitioned together: "Remonstrators of old came from reclusion or the army, yet all stood out in conduct.
units.literal: Later when Fengji fell, an edict made Su acting Remonstrator of the Left; chancellors Cui Qun and Wang Ya jointly petitioned: "The remonstrator of old was sometimes taken from mountain forests or promoted from the ranks, yet all were outstanding in conduct for their age.

units.zh: 今宿望輕，若待以不次，未足以寵，適以累之也。」
units.en: Su's standing is light; an exceptional appointment will not honor him—only harm him."
units.literal: Now Su's reputation is slight; if you favor him with an extraordinary appointment, it is not enough to honor him—it only harms him."

units.zh: 請授他官，不聽，使中人宣授焉。
units.en: They asked another post; the emperor refused and a eunuch proclaimed the appointment.
units.literal: They asked another office be given; the emperor would not listen and had a eunuch announce the appointment.

units.zh: 宿怨執政不與己，乃日肆讒甚，與皇甫镈相附離，多中傷正人君子。
units.en: Su hated the chancellors for not backing him and daily slandered, clinging to Huangfu Bo and wounding upright men.
units.literal: Su resented the rulers for not siding with him and daily poured out slander, attaching himself to Huangfu Bo and striking at upright gentlemen.

units.zh: 元和末，持節至淄青，李師道願割地遣子入侍。
units.en: Late in Yuanhe he bore credentials to Ziqing; Li Shidao offered to yield land and send his son to court.
units.literal: At the end of Yuanhe he held credentials to Ziqing; Li Shidao wished to cede territory and send his son to court as hostage.

units.zh: 既而悔，復遣宿往，暴卒於道，贈秘書監。
units.en: He then regretted it and sent Su again; Su died suddenly on the road and was posthumously made Secretariat Director.
units.literal: Then he repented and sent Su again; Su died violently on the road and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 熊望者，字原師，擢進士第。
units.en: Xiong Wang, style name Yuanshi, took the jinshi.
units.literal: Xiong Wang, styled Yuanshi, passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 性險躁，以辯說遊公卿間。
units.en: He was rash and treacherous, moving among grandees by debate.
units.literal: His nature was dangerous and impetuous; he traveled among dukes and ministers by eloquence.

units.zh: 劉棲楚為京兆尹，樹權勢，望日出入門下，為刺取事機，陰佐計畫。
units.en: As Qichu built power as Jingzhao magistrate, Wang came and went daily, picking up intelligence and plotting in secret.
units.literal: When Liu Qichu was metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao he built power; Wang daily entered his gate, spying out affairs and secretly aiding his schemes.

units.zh: 敬宗喜為歌詩，議置東頭學士，以備燕狎。
units.en: Jingzong loved verse and talked of Eastern Head academicians for private amusement.
units.literal: Jingzong delighted in composing songs and poems and discussed establishing Eastern Head Academicians for intimate revelry.

units.zh: 棲楚薦望，未及用，帝崩。
units.en: Qichu recommended Wang, but before the post was filled the emperor died.
units.literal: Qichu recommended Wang, but before appointment the emperor died.

units.zh: 文宗立，韋處厚秉政，詔望因緣險薄，營密職，圖褻幸，讙沸眾議，貶漳州司戶參軍。
units.en: Under Wenzong, Wei Chuhou ruled and condemned Wang for scheming toward secret posts and imperial intimacy; the uproar sent him to Zhangzhou as army aide.
units.literal: When Wenzong took the throne Wei Chuhou held government and issued an edict that Wang, by treacherous shallowness, sought secret office and imperial favor, stirring public clamor, be demoted to Zhangzhou army aide.

units.zh: 柏耆者，有縱橫學。
units.en: Bai Ji mastered alliance and stratagem.
units.literal: Bai Ji possessed the arts of alliance and stratagem.

units.zh: 父良器，為時威名將。
units.en: His father Liangqi was a renowned general of the time.
units.literal: His father Liangqi was a famed general of the age.

units.zh: 耆誌健而望高，急於立名。
units.en: Ji was vigorous and ambitious, hungry for renown.
units.literal: Ji was ambitious in spirit and high in reputation, eager to make a name.

units.zh: 是時，王承宗以常山叛，朝廷厭兵，耆杖策詣淮西行營謁裴度，且言願得天子一節馳入鎮，可掉舌下之。
units.en: Wang Chengzong had rebelled at Changshan while the court wearied of war; Ji visited Pei Du's western Huainan headquarters and vowed that with a single imperial commission he could talk the garrison into submission.
units.literal: At that time Wang Chengzong rebelled at Changshan; the court was weary of war. Ji took staff in hand, went to Pei Du's Huainan west circuit camp, and said he wished to obtain one imperial credential to gallop into the garrison and could bring it down with a wag of the tongue.

units.zh: 度為言，乃以左拾遺往。
units.en: Du endorsed him, and he went out as Left Reminder.
units.literal: Du spoke for him, and he was sent as Left Reminder.

units.zh: 既至，以大誼動承宗，至泣下。
units.en: He moved Chengzong with lofty argument until the rebel wept.
units.literal: Once he arrived, he moved Chengzong with great righteousness until Chengzong wept.

units.zh: 乃請獻二州，以二子入質。
units.en: Chengzong then offered two prefectures and sent two sons as hostages.
units.literal: Chengzong then offered to surrender two prefectures and send two sons as hostages.

units.zh: 真擢耆左拾遺，由是聲震一時。
units.en: The throne made him Left Reminder, and his name thundered across the realm.
units.literal: The emperor promoted Ji to Left Reminder, and from this his fame shook the age.

units.zh: 遷起居舍人。
units.en: He became Palace Diarist.
units.literal: He was transferred to Diarist of the Palace.

units.zh: 王承元徙義成軍，遣諫議大夫鄭覃往慰成德軍，賚緡錢百萬。
units.en: Wang Chengyuan was shifted to Yicheng; Remonstrator Zheng Tan was sent to comfort Chengde with a million strings of cash.
units.literal: When Wang Chengyuan was moved to the Yicheng army, Remonstrator of the Left Zheng Tan was sent to comfort the Chengde army, bearing a million strings of cash.

units.zh: 賚未至，舉軍嘩議，穆宗遣耆諭天子意，眾乃信悅。
units.en: The bounty had not arrived when the army erupted; Muzong sent Ji to proclaim the emperor's intent, and the troops were reassured.
units.literal: Before the gift arrived the whole army clamored; Muzong sent Ji to explain the Son of Heaven's intent, and the host then trusted and rejoiced.

units.zh: 轉兵部郎中、諫議大夫。
units.en: He rose to War Director and Left Remonstrator.
units.literal: He was made Director in the Ministry of War and Remonstrator of the Left.

units.zh: 太和初，李同捷反，詔兩河諸鎮出兵，久無功。
units.en: Early in Taihe, Li Tongjie rebelled; troops from the two He circuits were ordered out, yet victory lingered.
units.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Li Tongjie rebelled; an edict ordered the two He circuits to raise troops, but for long there was no success.

units.zh: 乃授耆德州行營諸軍計會使，與判官沈亞之諭旨。
units.en: Ji was appointed commissary of the Dezhou field armies and, with aide Shen Yazhi, delivered the throne's orders.
units.literal: Ji was then made Commissary for the Dezhou campaign armies of the two He circuits, and with judicial aide Shen Yazhi conveyed the imperial will.

units.zh: 會橫海節度使李祐平德州，同捷窮，請降，祐使大將萬洪代守滄州，同捷未出也，耆以三百騎馳入滄，以事誅洪，與同捷朝京師。
units.en: Li You of Transverse Sea took Dezhou; Tongjie, desperate, offered to yield. You left Wan Hong to hold Cangzhou while Tongjie lingered; Ji raced in with three hundred riders, killed Hong, and brought Tongjie to court.
units.literal: When Transverse Sea military commissioner Li You pacified Dezhou, Tongjie was cornered and sought surrender; You had great general Wan Hong hold Cangzhou in his stead while Tongjie had not yet departed. Ji galloped into Cang with three hundred horsemen, executed Hong on the facts of the case, and escorted Tongjie to the capital.

units.zh: 既行，諜言王廷湊欲以奇兵劫同捷，耆遂斬其首以獻。
units.en: As they marched, word came that Wang Tingcou would ambush Tongjie; Ji beheaded Tongjie and presented the head.
units.literal: After they set out, spies said Wang Tingcou meant to seize Tongjie with surprise troops; Ji then cut off his head and presented it.

units.zh: 諸將嫉耆功，比奏攢詆，文宗不獲已，貶耆循州司戶參軍、亞之南康尉。
units.en: Generals jealous of Ji's glory piled accusations; Wenzong, constrained, demoted Ji to Xunzhou army aide and Yazhi to Nan Kang aide.
units.literal: The generals envied Ji's merit and jointly memorialized slander; Wenzong, unable to refuse, demoted Ji to Xunzhou army aide and Yazhi to Nan Kang aide.

units.zh: 宦人馬國亮譖耆受同捷先所得王稷女及奴婢珍貲。
units.en: The eunuch Ma Guoliang accused Ji of taking Tongjie's spoils—Wang Ji's daughter and treasured slaves.
units.literal: Eunuch Ma Guoliang slandered Ji for taking Tongjie's prior prize—the daughter of Wang Ji—and slave girls with precious goods.

units.zh: 初，祐聞耆殺洪，大驚，疾遂劇。
units.en: When You first heard Ji had killed Hong, he was stunned and his illness worsened.
units.literal: Earlier, when You heard Ji had killed Hong, he was greatly shocked and his illness grew severe.

units.zh: 帝曰：「祐若死，是耆殺之。」
units.en: The emperor said, "If You dies, Ji has killed him."
units.literal: The emperor said: "If You dies, it is Ji who killed him."

units.zh: 至是，積前怒，詔長流愛州，賜死。
units.en: Now, anger piled upon anger, an edict banished him to Aizhou and commanded him to take his own life.
units.literal: By then, with prior anger accumulated, an edict exiled him far to Aizhou and ordered death by gift.

units.zh: 贊曰：詩人斥譖人最甚，投之豺虎、有北，不置也。
units.en: The commentator says: The Odes condemn slanderers most fiercely—throw them to wolves and tigers, drive them to the northern wilds, show no mercy.
units.literal: The commentator says: The poets rebuke slanderers most harshly—cast them to wolves and tigers, send them to the northern waste, do not spare them.

units.zh: 如群、棲楚輩則然，肆訐以示公，構黨以植私，其言纚纚若可聽，卒而入於敗亂也。
units.en: Men such as Qun and Qichu do the same—parade accusation as public duty, knit factions for private ends; their speech glides like truth, yet ends in ruin.
units.literal: Men like Qun and Qichu are just so: they freely accuse to show public virtue and build factions to plant private gain; their words flow smoothly as if worth hearing, yet in the end they enter ruin and disorder.

units.zh: 孔子所謂「順非而澤」者歟，「利口覆邦家」者歟？
units.en: Are they not Confucius's "pliant in wrong yet glossy of tongue" and "clever mouths that overturn kingdom and house"?
units.literal: Are they not those Confucius called "smooth-tongued in wrong" and "sharp-mouthed overturners of state and clan"?

units.zh: 耆掩眾取功，自速其死，哀哉！
units.en: Ji stole the army's credit and rushed to his doom—how lamentable!
units.literal: Ji concealed the host to seize merit and hastened his own death—pitiful!
